entries.content_plain:
Introduction

 Sennacherib invades Judea, 2Chr 32:1 . Hezekiah takes proper measures for the defense of his kingdom, 2Chr 32:2-6 . His exhortation, 2Chr 32:7 , 2Chr 32:8 . Sennacherib sends a blasphemous message to Hezekiah, and to the people, 2Chr 32:9-15 . His servants rail against God; and he and they blaspheme most grievously, 2Chr 32:16-19 . Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah cry to God; he answers, and the Assyrians are destroyed, and Sennacherib is slain by his own sons, 2Chr 32:20 , 2Chr 32:21 . The Lord is magnified, 2Chr 32:22 , 2Chr 32:23 . Hezekiah's sickness and recovery, 2Chr 32:24 . His ingratitude, 2Chr 32:25 . His humiliation, 2Chr 32:26 . His riches, 2Chr 32:27-30 . His error relative to the Babylonish ambassadors, 2Chr 32:31 . His acts and death, 2Chr 32:32 , 2Chr 32:33 . 

 Verse 1 

 After these things - God did not permit this pious prince to be disturbed till he had completed the reformation which he had begun.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 4</hi> <div eID="gen14574" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14575" type="x-p"/> Stopped all the fountains - This was prudently done, for without water how could an immense army subsist in an arid country? No doubt the Assyrian army suffered much through this, as a Christian army did eighteen hundred years after this. When the crusaders came, in a.d. 1099, to besiege Jerusalem, the people of the city stopped up the wells, so that the Christian army was reduced to the greatest necessities and distress.

entries.content_plain:
Verse 33 

 Chiefest of the sepulchres - This respect they paid to him who, since David, had been the best of all their kings. 

 I shall subjoin a few things from the Targum on this chapter. 2Chr 32:1 . "After these things which Hezekiah did, and their establishment, the Lord appointed by his Word to bring Sennacherib, king of Assyria, and his army, into the land of Israel, that he might destroy the Assyrians in the land of the house of Judah, and smite their troops on the mountains of Jerusalem, and deliver all their spoils into the hands of Hezekiah and his people: wherefore Sennacherib came with immense armies, which could not be numbered; and having pitched his camps in the land of the tribe of Judah, besieged their fortified cities with his armies, hoping to overthrow them." 2Chr 32:8 . Hezekiah said-"His help is the strength of the flesh; but our auxiliary is the Word of the Lord." 2Chr 32:16 . "His (Sennacherib's) servants spoke blasphemy against the Word of the Lord God." 2Chr 32:18 . In the Jews' speech - "In the language of the holy house." 2Chr 32:21 . "And the Word of the Lord sent Michael, and the angel Gabriel, and destroyed them on the night of the passover with a destructive fire; and burnt up their breath within their bodies, and consumed every soldier, captain, and prince, in the army of the king of Assyria; and he returned with shame of face into his own land." 

 The destruction of God's enemies, and the support and salvation of the faithful, is in every instance in this Targum attributed to the Word of the Lord, personally understood. See the note on 2Chr 34:27 . 2Chr 32:24 . "In those days was Hezekiah sick near to death; but he prayed before the Lord who spoke to him by his Word to preserve him and to add to his life fifteen years." 2Chr 32:31 . "The king of Babylon sent, that they might inquire concerning the miracle that had been done in the land; that they might see the two tables of stone which were in the ark of the covenant of the Lord which Moses had placed there with the two tables which he had broken on account of the sin of the calf which they made in Horeb. The Word of the Lord permitted him to show them these; neither did he suffer for it; that he might try him, and see what was in his heart." 

 Thus God speaks after the manner of men: he either brings, or permits them to be brought, into such circumstances as shall cause them to show their prevailing propensities; and then warns them against the evils to which they are inclined, after having shown them that they are capable of those evils. To know ourselves, and our own character, is of the utmost importance to our religious growth and perfection. He who does not know where his weakness lies, is not likely to know where his strength lies. Many, by not being fully acquainted with their own character, have been unwatchful and unguarded, and so become an easy prey to their enemies. Know thyself is a lesson which no man can learn but from the Spirit of God.
